sourceNote: The hippo mesh (assets/models/hippo/hippo.glb, assets/models/hippo/README.md), with new quad faces on each arm from the arm seam to the wrist, a side wall of the trunk under each arm, and arms 1.5 times longer. tools/blender/hippo_arms.py replays the Blender session that made it. hippo.glb stays unchanged.
paintedNote: The weights of the clavicles and the arms are the automatic weights of Blender with the Weight Paint fixes of tools/blender/hippo_arms.py. The vertices on the bones of paintedLower keep the rule weights, because the seated bind of the app depends on them.

armSegments.rootSegmentNote: The rule weight of each upper arm goes to its first segment (segment_joints() and main() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py), so that the trunk around the socket takes the roll of the first ring of the tube, as on the fox.
armSegments.note: Each upper arm and each forearm has 4 deform segments, and each elbow and wrist a helper bone of this length in units. The app turns them from the pose joints (poseArm() of src/models/studio-rig.ts), so the length changes only the automatic weights of Blender. A longer helper folds more play samples.

armSmooth.note: 6 rounds of taubin() smooth the middle of each arm tube after the weights (arm_smooth() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py), so that the arms show no lumps or dents. The elbow rings and the root stay out, because the elbow rings keep a gap for the helper bone and the root joins the side wall.

bindSmooth.note: 12 rounds of taubin() smooth the bind mesh of the left elbow after its relax (arm_smooth() on the bind, main() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). The seated bind bends the left elbow far, and without this rule the inner elbow folds into a lip.

raise.note: The rest shape of the right arm: the mean turns of the rest samples of the bassist. It smooths the posed tube from the second upper arm segment to the wrist (raise_shape() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py), with no relax (below -1). The fade keeps it off the play.

name: Hippo

app.note: The scale puts the standing skull top (the highest vertex within 0.03 u of the middle plane) at 1.570 m, the head height of the red fox: 1.600907 m for each unit, with the standing shoulder joints at 0.888504 m (ANIMALS).

armFactorNote: The factor 1 does not stretch the arms in the rig. The arms of hippo-arms.glb are already 1.5 times longer than the source arms (step_shape() of tools/blender/violin_arms.py, called by tools/blender/hippo_arms.py). The contrabass of the hippo is smaller (bassScale 0.8 of src/models/species.ts).
legFactorNote: The legs keep the length of the mesh. The hippo stands at its contrabass in the app, as the hippos of the reference images, so no seat asks for longer legs.

rootNormals.note: The skin faces whose middle lies within radius (units) of the head of an upper arm take the skin normals with no crease angle in the app (root_rim() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). The seated bind turns the arm up, and without this rule a hard dark crease shows under the left arm.
rootNormals.armShareNote: A face of the radius stays in the rim only when the mean weight of its corners on the clavicle and the arm bones of its side is 0.3 or more (root_rim()). Thus the big trunk faces under the left armpit keep their own normals and show no dark patch.
rootNormals.turnNote: A face of the rim keeps the crease normals when a corner takes a skin normal more than 60 degrees from its own face in the final bind (rim_turns()). Thus the big trunk face under the right armpit shows no black wedge under the bow arm.
rootNormals.elbowNote: The faces within 0.09 units of each elbow joint take the skin normals (root_rim() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). The left paw on the neck bends the left elbow far, and without this rule the split normals show a thin dark line across the elbow.

jointsNote: The places are in the studio units and axes of the source pose: 1 unit from the soles to the ear tops, +z forward, +x the left side. The neck joint lies below the chin. The elbow, forearm twist, wrist, and paw joints are the joints of the longer arms.

studio.note: legTurns gives the world turn of each left leg bone from the seated bind to the source (tools/rig/leg_turns.py <config> 25 15 0). The bind hand bends 25 degrees off the forearm in the palm plane, as the source paw, and the bow paw keeps this bend (HIPPO_HOLD.pawKeepR of src/pose/bowed-rig.ts).

weights.armBelowNote: Inside the plane of armSplit, the share of the arm weight that a vertex keeps grows from 0 at the lower height to 1 at the upper height (units), and the trunk takes the rest. This ramp folds the root of the arm tube the least.

sliver.note: The values of the fox, the cat, the dog, and the panda.

line.note: The values of the fox, the cat, the dog, and the panda.

weights.clavicleMiddleNote: The share of the clavicle weight that a vertex below headFrom keeps grows from 0 at the smaller distance from the middle plane to 1 at the larger distance (units), and the chest takes the rest. Thus the bow arm does not fold the chest under the chin.
weights.armTopNote: The share of the clavicle and upper arm weights that a vertex gives to the neck grows from 0 at the lower height to 1 at the upper height (units). The wide fade keeps the back of the right shoulder from a fold. The fade is sensitive to small changes.
weights.rigidNote: The face nearest to each point (source units) takes the mean of the weights of its corners. Face 323 at the back of the right side of the neck joins the head, the neck, and the clavicle, and without this rule the bow arm folds it (pnpm fold-probe bassist --faces).

haunch.note: The part of the thigh weight that goes to the hips grows from 0 at the lower height to 1 at the upper height, so that the round haunch stays on the hips. It starts at the knee and ends at the crotch.

weights.note: Beyond the plane |x| = armSplit, only the free arm follows the arm bones. The plane lies out of the whole trunk, so that no trunk vertex takes a lower arm bone. The arm vertices take the weights of Blender (paintedWeights). Above headFrom (the chin), each vertex follows the head only.

flip.note: The rule of the fox, the rabbit, the cat, the dog, and the panda, with a lower angle, a larger move, and wider normals (refine.flipNote).

refine.ringsNote: The rig has no rings. A ring at each elbow or at a wrist puts the rig above 3,200 triangles.
refine.flipNote: The long edge of each thin face of the arms in the seated bind flips (flip_edges() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). The bind bends the thick elbows 62 degrees, so the inner elbow faces are thin. The angle 130, the move 0.004, and the normals 90 flip more of them.

check.note: The values of the fox, the cat, the dog, and the panda.

tone.note: The mesh has warmer colors than SPECIES_COLORS.hippo. Each plain face takes the hue and the chroma of the species color of its band and keeps its lightness: a row is [L, dL, da, db] in Oklab. The claws keep their colors.

colors.note: The values of samples, palette, dark, and eyeShare are the values of the other meshes. A dark face in the eye box is an eye face. The config has no nose box, because the hippo has no nose pad: the export takes the front of the muzzle as the nose tip.

eyeShell.note: The values of the fox, the cat, and the dog. The old eye of each side is its dark faces and the faces around them, and they take the color of the faces around them.

chair.note: The chair of the rig sets the seat top of the seated bind under the haunch. The short thighs lie under the belly, so the seat ends behind them. The hippo stands in the app (soloist of ANIMALS), so no player sits on this seat.

crease.note: The values of the cat, the dog, and the panda.

sit.note: The values of the panda: the haunch moves down at most 0.03 u.
